sections.name: File setup, GET, packetPatchSchema, PATCH
sections.title: Packet read and edit handlers
sections.what: Returns one packet for its case and lets the user edit notes or request text through PATCH, with the body checked against a rule.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps edits limited to allowed fields and to the owning case.
sections.watch_out: Only READY_FOR_REVIEW is accepted as a status value, so other status changes are refused.

summary: Web address to read one review packet and to edit its citizen notes or requested review text while it is still a draft.
purpose: Lets a user view a prepared review packet and add notes or a request.
why: Likely reason: a packet is a snapshot, so edits are allowed only before it is marked ready.
how: GET looks up the packet by case and packet id and returns it, or a 404 if not found. PATCH reads a body with optional notes and request text, each up to 4000 characters, plus an optional status that may only be READY_FOR_REVIEW. Invalid input returns 400. The rest of PATCH is cut off in the source, but tests show a locked packet returns 409.
inputs: Case id and packet id in the address. PATCH body with optional citizenNotes, requestedReviewText, and status.
outputs: Packet data, or errors with codes INVALID_INPUT, PACKET_NOT_FOUND, and PACKET_LOCKED.
risks: The end of PATCH is cut off, so the locking logic is confirmed only through the tests. Text is capped at 4000 characters.
debug: A 409 means the packet is locked. A 404 means the packet does not belong to that case.
